analysis.title: Prime HFs Update - Oct 22nd - Broad based de-grossing driven by long selling
key_insights: Hedge funds have de-grossed in 7 of the past 8 sessions across global equities, and the pace is accelerating. The last such streak was in April 2026, and none occurred in 2025.
Oct 22 was the 5th largest de-grossing event of 2026 at -1.6 SD, driven entirely by long selling. It was the largest long selling since September 2025.

Almost all major regions saw risk unwinds on Oct 22, led by North America (long sales), Europe (long sales > short covers) and EM Asia (long sales > short sales). China and Hong Kong were the most net sold Asian markets, while Taiwan, Korea and Japan were sold at a more moderate pace.
9 of 11 global sectors saw risk unwinds, led by Info Tech and Industrials.

Info Tech saw long selling alongside short additions, the largest net selling since September 2024. Every industry was net sold, led by Semi & Semi Equipment, which was also the most de-grossed. Fundamental L/S funds did most of the de-grossing, with multi-strats and quants also selling. Semi allocations have dropped back to levels seen earlier in the year.
Industrials was de-grossed mainly by multi-strats and quants, with every industry de-grossed. Oct 22 was the third largest industrials de-grossing day of the year.
Global AI basket (GSXGGLAI) names saw the largest net selling since end of July. Net and gross allocations have fallen back to the lows seen after the July moves.

Prime book gross leverage was 312.3% (-0.4 pts DoD), at the 79th percentile over 1 year and 96th over 5 years. Net leverage was 71.8% (-2.1 pts DoD), at the 3rd percentile over 1 year and 37th over 5 years.
Global Fundamental L/S gross leverage was 211.7% (-0.4 pts DoD) and net leverage 47% (-3.1 pts DoD), at the 1st percentile over 3 years and 5th over 5 years.

At the Oct 22 US close, more than two-thirds of hedge funds finished down as concentrated shorts squeezed in the second half of the session. For the first time since COVID, all three broad equity strategies fell more than 1% on the same day.

Global Fundamental L/S fell 1.4% (-2.1 SD) on Oct 22, the worst day since July 16. Alpha of -0.5% came from China and Info Tech exposures and the squeeze in concentrated shorts. The group is down 3.8% MTD and up 8.8% YTD.
TMT-focused funds fell 2.7% (-1.9 SD) on Oct 22, down 9.6% MTD and up 8.0% YTD.

Global Systematic L/S fell 1.3% (-3.4 SD) on Oct 22, the third-worst day since December 2023. All three of those days fell in roughly the past two months (Aug 19, Oct 15 and Oct 22). The group is up 19.0% YTD.

Multi-strats (equity portfolio, 4.5x leverage) fell 1.9% (-3.2 SD) on Oct 22, driven by Momentum, Info Tech, Concentrated Shorts and Crowded Longs. It was the second-worst day since the April 2025 tariff sell-off, behind only July 28.
At noon on Oct 22, Momentum was down 2.6 SD and Crowded Longs down 2.8 SD, the worst daily sell-off since the week of Liberation Day in April 2025.

On Oct 15 (AI sell-off), Momentum was down 3.4 SD, Crowded Longs down 1.8 SD and Crowded Shorts squeezed +1.2 SD intraday. Global Systematic L/S closed down 1.4% (-3.7 SD), the worst day since Aug 19.
From COVID through end-2025, all three broad strategies never fell more than 80bps on the same day. In 2026 it has happened three times: Feb 4, Jul 28 and Oct 15.

sector_views.rationale: Largest net selling since September 2024 on Oct 22, with long selling alongside short additions and every industry net sold. Semi & Semi Equipment was the most de-grossed.
Third largest de-grossing day of the year on Oct 22, primarily by multi-strats and quants, with every industry de-grossed.

risk_factors: Continued de-grossing by fundamental L/S, multi-strat and quant funds, led by long selling in Info Tech, semis and AI names.
Momentum and crowded-long factor unwinds, with concentrated shorts squeezing against funds.
Clustering of large simultaneous losses across all three broad hedge fund strategies, which has happened three times in 2026 after never occurring from COVID through 2025.

Global Fundamental L/S gross leverage is 211.7% (63rd percentile 1-year, 92nd percentile 5-year). Net leverage is 47% (1st percentile 3-year, 5th percentile 5-year).
